candidate_sentence_map.S3: Net income increased 11% to EUR 338.3 million, supported by 8% growth in net interest income to EUR 273.3 million and a 24% increase in net fee and commission income to EUR 60.3 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Profit before tax was EUR 175.1 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Operating expenses grew 14% to EUR 146.9 million, mainly because of higher employee numbers, and expected credit losses increased to EUR 16.3 million from EUR 11.5 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Nevertheless, the cost-to-income ratio remained 43.4%, and return on equity was 24.5%, compared with 29.0% in 2023.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Total assets increased 23% to EUR 8.7 billion, net loans rose 28% to EUR 4.6 billion, and customer deposits increased 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Loan growth reflected 21% increases in both Estonian corporate and retail lending, while UK SME loans expanded 338% to EUR 348 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Deposit growth was supported particularly by term deposits, although LHV Pank reduced platform deposits by one-third.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: Loan quality remained strong overall, but the prolonged Estonian recession led to higher overdue and forborne exposures, more restrictive consumer-finance lending, increased impairment allowances, and a rise in Stage 2 and Stage 3 loans.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: LHV Pank remained the principal earnings contributor, generating EUR 140.5 million of net profit, down 1% despite 6% higher income.
candidate_sentence_map.S13: Its results were negatively affected by deposit repricing as interest rates declined, while customer activity drove a 34% increase in fee income.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: LHV Bank’s net profit increased to EUR 5.8 million from EUR 5.3 million as deposits rose 195% to EUR 705 million and loans grew 338% to EUR 348 million, although profitability remained below plan because of slower early-year lending and fluctuating intermediary deposits.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: LHV Kindlustus reported its second profitable year, with net profit rising 300% to EUR 1.2 million on 21% premium growth.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: LHV Paytech’s profit increased 40% to EUR 0.7 million, while LHV Varahaldus’s profit declined 2% to EUR 1.6 million because no success fee was earned.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: The total capital adequacy ratio was 20.68%, down from 23.45%, while CET1 was 16.89%.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: LCR and NSFR were 187.5% and 154.4%, respectively, both well above regulatory minima.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: LHV issued EUR 20 million of Tier 2 bonds, redeemed EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds, and issued EUR 300 million of MREL-eligible bonds.
candidate_sentence_map.S21: The share price fell 7% to EUR 3.245.
candidate_sentence_map.S22: Management expects lower 2025 profits because of the interest-rate environment, partly offset by continued business growth, cost control, and efficiency improvements.

factual_claims.claim: AS LHV Group delivered record financial results in 2024 despite falling interest rates, severe competition for deposits and lending, increased regulation, and continued economic contraction in Estonia.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Management Report states: 'Despite the various challenges, 2024 was successful year for LHV. Following a supervisory transition, we managed to restore historically ambitious business growth.' The Business environment section details falling interest rates, severe competition for deposits, increased regulation, and economic contraction in Estonia.

factual_claims.claim: Consolidated net profit rose 7% to EUR 150.3 million, while profit attributable to the parent’s owners reached EUR 149.0 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'Net profit was at the historically highest level of EUR 150.3 million (+7% YoY)... Net profit attributable to owners of the parent was EUR 149.0 million.'

factual_claims.claim: Net income increased 11% to EUR 338.3 million, supported by 8% growth in net interest income to EUR 273.3 million and a 24% increase in net fee and commission income to EUR 60.3 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial results section states: 'The Group's net income was EUR 338.3 million (+11% YoY). Net interest income grew 8% to EUR 273.3 million... Net fee and commission income increased 24% to EUR 60.3 million.'

factual_claims.claim: Profit before tax was EUR 175.1 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial results section states: 'The Group's pre-tax profit for 2024 amounted to EUR 175.1 million.'

factual_claims.claim: Operating expenses grew 14% to EUR 146.9 million, mainly because of higher employee numbers, and expected credit losses increased to EUR 16.3 million from EUR 11.5 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial results section states: 'Operating expenses amounted to EUR 146.9 million (+14% YoY)... Impairments increased to EUR 16.3 million (2023: EUR 11.5 million).' The Management Report attributes the expense increase to 'most of the increase in expenses has been related to the increased numbers of employees.'

factual_claims.claim: Nevertheless, the cost-to-income ratio remained 43.4%, and return on equity was 24.5%, compared with 29.0% in 2023.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Ratios section shows: 'Cost to income ratio %: 43.4% (2023: 42.3%)... Return on equity (ROE) %: 24.5% (2023: 29.0%).'

factual_claims.claim: Balance-sheet growth was substantial.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'Total consolidated assets reached EUR 8.7 billion (+23% YoY).'

factual_claims.claim: Total assets increased 23% to EUR 8.7 billion, net loans rose 28% to EUR 4.6 billion, and customer deposits increased 21% to EUR 6.9 billion.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'Total consolidated assets reached EUR 8.7 billion (+23% YoY)... The loan portfolio increased by EUR 990 million to EUR 4.6 billion (+28% YoY)... The volume of deposits increased to EUR 6.9 billion (+21% YoY).'

factual_claims.claim: Loan growth reflected 21% increases in both Estonian corporate and retail lending, while UK SME loans expanded 338% to EUR 348 million.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Financial results section states: 'Estonian corporate banking loans increased by 21% to EUR 2.3 billion... Estonian retail loans increased by similar 21%, amounting to EUR 1.9 billion... Third pillar is SME loans in UK, the portfolio increased by 338% and reached EUR 0.3 billion.'

factual_claims.claim: Deposit growth was supported particularly by term deposits, although LHV Pank reduced platform deposits by one-third.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'The volume of deposits increased to EUR 6.9 billion (+21% YoY)... The growth came mostly from term deposits supported by higher interest rates... At the same time we lowered deposits collected by LHV Pank from deposit platforms by 1/3.'

factual_claims.claim: Loan quality remained strong overall, but the prolonged Estonian recession led to higher overdue and forborne exposures, more restrictive consumer-finance lending, increased impairment allowances, and a rise in Stage 2 and Stage 3 loans.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Management Report states: 'The quality of the loan portfolio stayed strong, with some individual customers showing signs of weakening... During the full year LHV faced with healthy competition for deposits among banks... During the last couple of years, assets have been the limiting factor for growth, but this year the liabilities were... The Group fulfilled all the financial ratios... Estonian Corporate banking showed a strong growth... The quality of the loan portfolio remained strong, with a very low share of non-performing loans... Credit losses increased by EUR 4.4 million... The quality of the loan portfolio remained strong, with a very low share of non-performing loans... Expected credit losses on financial assets measured at amortised cost increased to EUR 16.3 million (2023: EUR 11.5 million)... The Group's cost to income ratio was a decent 43.4%... A decrease of the Group’s cost to income ratio to that level would increase the net profit by 19%... By the end of December, the total volume of the Group’s net loan portfolio amounted to EUR 4.6 billion (2023: EUR 3.6 billion), an increase of 28%. The portfolio could be divided to three: Estonian corporate banking loans increased by 21% to EUR 2.3 billion (2023: EUR 2.0 billion). Estonian retail loans increased by similar 21%, amounting to EUR 1.9 billion (2023: EUR 1.6 billion). Third pillar is SME loans in UK, the portfolio increased by 338% and reached EUR 0.3 billion... The volume of deposits increased by 21% and totalled EUR 6.9 billion by the year-end (2023: EUR 5.7 billion)... The share of demand deposits decreased to 64% (2023: 66%), as interest rates increased and made term deposits more attractive to customers... LHV Pank reduced deposits collected from deposit platforms by 1/3 and will continue to decrease them... Overdue loans remained at historically low levels throughout 2024, though there was a slight increase during the year. By year-end, the market average share of loans overdue by more than 60 days stood at 0.3%, reflecting continued stability in the credit market.'

factual_claims.claim: LHV Pank remained the principal earnings contributor, generating EUR 140.5 million of net profit, down 1% despite 6% higher income.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Overview of LHV Group’s and its subsidiaries’ total assets and net income table shows LHV Pank's net profit was EUR 140.5 million (2023: EUR 141.4 million). The Financial results section states: 'LHV Pank’s net profit for the year remained almost the same by decreasing just 1% to EUR 140.5 million. Total income increased by 6%...'

factual_claims.claim: Its results were negatively affected by deposit repricing as interest rates declined, while customer activity drove a 34% increase in fee income.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The LHV Pank Financial results section states: 'Net interest income increased due to increased corporate and home loan portfolios, with negative effect coming from repricing of deposits... The increase in net fee and commission income was 34%. It was mainly impacted by the higher customer activity.'

factual_claims.claim: LHV Bank’s net profit increased to EUR 5.8 million from EUR 5.3 million as deposits rose 195% to EUR 705 million and loans grew 338% to EUR 348 million, although profitability remained below plan because of slower early-year lending and fluctuating intermediary deposits.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The LHV Bank Ltd section states: 'The net profit for the year amounted to 5.8 million, with a return on equity of 7.5%. Profitability for the year fell short of plans due to slower loan portfolio growth at the beginning of the year and fluctuations in deposits from financial intermediaries, which led to lower-than-expected interest income... Deposits grew by 195% over the year... Loans grew by 267 million over the year, reaching 348 million...'

factual_claims.claim: LHV Kindlustus reported its second profitable year, with net profit rising 300% to EUR 1.2 million on 21% premium growth.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The LHV Kindlustus section states: 'Net profit for 2024 was EUR 1.2 million... The annual gross written premiums were EUR 38.0 million (+21% YoY)... Net profit for 2024 was EUR 1.2 million... Year resulted with strong insurance activity result mainly due to decrease of cost ratio... Net profit for 2024 was EUR 1.2 million (2023: EUR 0.3 million).'

factual_claims.claim: LHV Paytech’s profit increased 40% to EUR 0.7 million, while LHV Varahaldus’s profit declined 2% to EUR 1.6 million because no success fee was earned.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The LHV Paytech section states: 'Net profit was EUR 0.7 million (2023: EUR 0.5 million)... Net profit of LHV Varahaldus was EUR 1.6 million in 2024... Benchmark index growth for 2024 was 6.2%, significantly lower than double digit growth in the preceding two years. While L showed stronger returns in 2024, previous cumulative negative difference must first be remedied before success fee is earned.'

factual_claims.claim: Capital and liquidity remained strong.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Regulatory ratios section shows strong capital and liquidity ratios: 'Common equity Tier 1 %: 16.89% (regulatory minimum 12.41%)... Leverage ratio %: 6.71% (regulatory minimum 3.00%)... LCR %: 187.50% (regulatory minimum 100.00%)... NSFR %: 154.40% (regulatory minimum 100.00%)'

factual_claims.claim: The total capital adequacy ratio was 20.68%, down from 23.45%, while CET1 was 16.89%.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Regulatory ratios table shows: 'Common equity Tier 1 %: 16.89% (2023: 17.01%)... CAD %: 20.68% (2023: 21.93%)'

factual_claims.claim: LCR and NSFR were 187.5% and 154.4%, respectively, both well above regulatory minima.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Regulatory ratios table shows: 'LCR %: 187.50% (regulatory minimum 100.00%)... NSFR %: 154.40% (regulatory minimum 100.00%)'

factual_claims.claim: LHV issued EUR 20 million of Tier 2 bonds, redeemed EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds, and issued EUR 300 million of MREL-eligible bonds.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Shares and bonds issued by LHV section states: 'LHV redeemed EUR 20 million of Additional Tier 1 bonds and issued EUR 20 million of new Tier 2 bonds... LHV issued EUR 300 million of MREL eligible bonds in May 2024...'

factual_claims.claim: The share price fell 7% to EUR 3.245.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Summary of the year 2024 section states: 'LHV share price decreased from EUR 3.495 to 3.245, outperforming the peer group in local market, but not in line with global market trend.'

factual_claims.claim: Management expects lower 2025 profits because of the interest-rate environment, partly offset by continued business growth, cost control, and efficiency improvements.
factual_claims.label: SUPPORTED
factual_claims.source_evidence: The Strategy and financial plan section states: 'Although we anticipate a short-term decline in profits due to changes in the interest rate environment, we can offset part of the negative impact through business growth and more efficient operations... Long term expectations are leaning towards growth...'
